The actual power variation on [0,N] is bounded by d*(L/N)*N^d, through true normalization of the existing power oscillation bound. For actual n=a+q*j, the true integer q divides the actual integer n^d-a^d, proved by genuine difference-of-powers divisibility.

If actual N^d*norm(q*alpha)<=B, true round(q*alpha) and the actual integer quotient of n^d-a^d remove the rational phase EXACTLY. The genuine remaining real error gives actual top-power phase variation<=2*pi*d*B*H/N along the same actual progression. No real scalar quotient-circle map or modular division is introduced.

Actual removal of the top monomial lowers the true degree bound and gives the exact real evaluation/phase factorization. The original sample phase error is exactly the actual top-monomial phase error, using a true unit lower phase. Actual affine polynomial substitution evaluates at the actual integer progression and preserves the true lower degree bound.

Actual pointwise errors between complex samples and a true constant unit factor times lower samples bound the actual finite mean difference. The genuine triangle inequality then retains a large lower mean. No phase alignment or approximation conclusion is assumed.

For an actual fixed fraction rho and rho*N>=2, the actual natural floor H is positive and satisfies rho*N/2<=H<=rho*N. Actual fixed positive fractions chosen from the degree, top bound and delta satisfy BOTH original tail-width and top-phase-error budgets before polynomial coefficients and N.

GENUINE top stripping is proved with B,M,rho chosen BEFORE the polynomial and N. All original indices, floor lengths, coefficient control and sample errors are retained. No conditional localization/existence input remains.

Actual Taylor coefficients are expanded by the true finite polynomial monomial sum, and true affine scaling multiplies coefficient j by q^j. A true weighted modular norm bound is proved using actual nearest integers and actual finite absolute-sum bounds. The SAME integer recovery gives original coefficient i error N^-i, with an actual uniform budget (D+1)*q^D*2^D*A/rho^D. The constant coefficient is not assumed controlled: its weight is exactly zero for every positive i.

The complete-block progression samples have actual positions q*H*b+r+q*j. The selected start a is an original natural integer a<N, and EVERY actual sample a+q*j, j<H, remains <N.

Actual finite maximum selection is applied to the true nested means after the genuine block-sum identity. Actual unit samples bound the tail before selection. The proof shows the actual prefix and outer block set are nonempty rather than assuming these properties. The actual block mean is retained at delta/2; no cancellation or common complex direction is assumed.

The top variation uses actual alpha, q, round(q*alpha) and the true integer quotient of (a+q*j)^d-a^d. It subtracts the true integer round(q*alpha)*quotient, proves equality of the actual circle values, and only then bounds the genuine real error. The top-stripping fraction is a fixed minimum of actual positive real budgets. Its floor length is chosen from rho*N after N, with a fixed positive M guaranteeing H>=rho*N/2. q<=B, the actual floor upper bound and the original width budget enforce the tail restriction; the same data enforce pointwise phase error<=delta/8. The coefficient recovery is an actual equality of real polynomial coefficients. It uses genuine Taylor translation, actual affine scaling and actual integer clearing by q^D. Every recovery weight is an explicitly defined true integer. Terms below i vanish by true choose(j,i)=0, so no nonconstant estimate accidentally calls a constant-coefficient hypothesis.

The recovery norm proof uses actual nearest integers for the actual affine coefficients, followed by the actual weighted finite norm inequality. Original a<=N gives actual integer weight growth N^(j-i). The true fractional-length transfer at H>=rho*N controls N^j times each actual affine error; summing after multiplication by N^i retains N^-i. All divisions have positive real rho powers. There is no modular division by q or H.

The simultaneous inverse is a genuine degree induction rooted in a vacuous degree-zero case. For degree D+1 it selects fixed top-stripping B,M,rho and fixed lower-degree K at delta/4 BEFORE p,N. The actual chosen q,a,H come from genuine top stripping; the lower-degree induction is applied to the actual polynomial on that actual progression. ONE actual k controls every lower coefficient. The output Q=k*q^(D+1) is positive and bounded before checking ALL original i. The same q controls the original top coefficient, and Q includes it even at D=0. Lower original coefficients are recovered with the SAME integer weights and multiplied by the extra q. Fixed ceiling budgets contain the lower and top errors. The separate bounded-N case uses Q=1 and controls every coefficient by the actual circle half-period bound. Thus no extra character, coefficient, progression or inverse existence hypothesis remains at the root.
